title.value: A Realistic Protocol for Evaluation of Weakly Supervised Object Localization
title.justification: The title explicitly mentions that the paper provides a realistic protocol for evaluating WSOL methods.
title.quote: A Realistic Protocol for Evaluation of Weakly Supervised Object Localization

analysis.description: This paper addresses the evaluation protocol for Weakly Supervised Object Localization (WSOL) by proposing a methodology that does not rely on ground truth bounding boxes for model selection or threshold estimation. By using pseudo-bounding boxes generated from pretrained region proposal methods like Selective Search, CLIP, and RPN, the authors provide a more realistic evaluation framework for WSOL methods. The paper demonstrates that using these pseudo-annotations can yield performance comparable to traditional methods that rely on ground truth annotations.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments with several WSOL methods on datasets like ILSVRC and CUB using the proposed protocol.
type.quote: Our experiments with several WSOL methods on ILSVRC and CUB datasets show that using the proposed pseudo-bboxes for validation facilitates the model selection and threshold estimation.
